analysis.title: US Equities Weekly Rundown: Positioning, Flows, and Observations Across the Floor (October 30, 2026)
key_insights: US stocks fell Friday but the S&P 500 closed the week and month only modestly lower. The market is bifurcating, with AI exposures selling off while select non-AI pockets (Obesity Drugs, Defense Spending, Biotech) outperform. Bitcoin Sensitive, Software and Agentic AI baskets lagged.
Hedge funds net bought US equities for the first time in 4 weeks (+1.1 SDs 1-year). The buying was driven by short covers in Macro Products (index and ETF), with Single Stocks a smaller contributor.

Info Tech was the most net bought sector this week but remains heavily net sold month to date. This week's buying through Thursday is about 40% of what HFs sold in the prior 3 weeks, and Mag 7 stocks were net sold in 4 of the last 5 sessions. The desk reads this as little recovery in risk appetite.
US Fundamental L/S net leverage rose 3.6 pts to 47%, the 7th percentile over one year, while gross leverage is 216.3%, the 66th percentile. Funds are heavily grossed up but lightly net long.

Shares desk: the week began with Long Only demand in Semis and ended with an aggressive sell-off and very little defense. Asset managers finished net sellers and HF flows were balanced. ETFs were about 31% of the tape, the highest full-session level since June, and the moves looked systematic and top-down. Month-end dynamics were also at work.

Key S&P levels the shares desk is watching are the 100-day moving average (7614) and the CTA medium-term threshold (7554). The derivatives desk says the S&P broke its medium-term CTA threshold (7544.2) on Friday.
Consumer outperformed Thursday and Friday on rotation out of tech into Staples, better restaurant and cruise earnings (CMG, WING, EAT, NCLH, RCL) and covering in under-owned names (CROX, BOOT).

Next week the S&P implied move through Friday 11/6 is 1.84%. The focus is on the last major week of Q3 earnings (AAPL Monday), the US midterm elections Tuesday (Kalshi prices 65% odds of a Democratic sweep), Wednesday's Treasury refunding details on tenors (watching 20y and 30y issuance) and Friday's jobs numbers.

Russell 2000 finished the week positive (+0.6% WoW at the time of writing), outperforming Nasdaq (-2.8%) and S&P 500 (-1.0%) on rate relief and resilient GDP. The futures desk says the rally was orderly short covering, and new length took profit rather than chasing.

The futures desk expects Russell 2000 upside to stay capped by rate sensitivity and debt-refinancing headwinds. If Friday's price action persists, GS systematic momentum thresholds flip negative, which would halt projected CTA buying.

Natural gas has diverged across the Atlantic since 9/30. December TTF is up 43% (above 100 EUR/MWh), UK NBP is up 39% and Henry Hub is down 15%. European gas is driven by Middle East supply disruptions and below-average storage, while US inventories are 1% (185 Bcf) above the 5-year average. US LNG producers are positioned to gain share, and Cheniere and Woodside signed major supply deals with Qatar Energy.

Sugar fell 5.6% on October 26 after a Brazilian election surprise weakened the BRL. Short-term CTA momentum briefly turned negative but the medium-term signal stayed positive. Put-call skew did not richen significantly, which the desk attributes to Super El Nino fears.

Derivatives desk: front-end vol fell sharply early in the week (NDX 1m fixed strike vol down almost 4 vol points), then reversed on Friday with the same tenor up almost 2 vol points. The realized move versus implied in QQQ was one of the most outsized on a 1-year lookback.
The derivatives desk says flows are catching up to the bear thesis for the first time. Friday activity was concentrated in buying downside at the index level and in Semis. VVIX surpassed 120.
Gamma has not repriced as much as vol and skew. The straddle through Wednesday's close, covering the midterms, priced 1.51% against a Friday S&P move of -1.82%.
Breadth was healthier than price action suggested. 406 SPX constituents were up on Thursday, one of the highest readings of 2026, and SPX ex-AI closed Friday in the green.
US pensions were modeled to buy $4.5bn of US equities into month-end, which ranks in the 31st percentile of buy and sell estimates over three years.

TMT: the NDX matched its biggest monthly decline since the start of the AI cycle (about -7% in October). Semis fell about 8% Friday, the 3rd largest day of underperformance in more than 15 years. Earnings catalysts were a mixed Kioxia guide, a large INTC guide down, uneven 2H hyperscaler capex and an AMKR smartphone downtick.

The TMT specialists say the AI demand engine (token demand and GW/data-center build-outs) is intact, but the market is more discerning on the linearity of the story beyond CY27, which pressures multiples until visibility improves. Investors are rotating into IBM, AAPL, SPOT, V/MA, EBAY and LYV.

Financials: the debate is where we are in the cycle and how much of the cycle depends on the AI infrastructure buildout. Banks and capital markets stocks were sold, and insurance stayed shorted on soft-cycle fears with P&C earnings showing pricing pressure. HFs de-grossed Financials for a second straight week at the fastest pace in more than 6 months.

Most debated Financials earnings: LPLA, senior housing REITs, SPGI (strategic review), MA and AMP. GPN was topical Friday on a Financial Times report of potential takeout interest. Next week's focus names are APO (AI platform exposure), MET and AFRM (rate sensitivity).

Industrials rose 210bps on the week and are above 300bps month to date, outperforming a market down about 50bps. Winners: HAYW +27%, BAH +14% (partly a short squeeze), TXT +12%, IP +9%, FTV similar. Losers: OI -22%, DAN -15%, TFII, LSTR and CHRW down 12-14%, and BA -9% after lowering expectations for free cash flow timing.

Healthcare outperformed and XLV hit a fresh all-time high on a defensive bid. Large biopharma led: LLY +7% (Mounjaro and Zepbound beat and guidance raise), REGN +11%, GILD +3.4%, MRK +4%. Medtech updates skewed to negative surprises on forward guidance.

Pre-midterm basket ideas by affordability theme: long ACA-exposed beneficiaries (GSHLCACA), short drug-makers (GSHLCBPH), long renewables, grid infrastructure and Power Up America, buy protection on hyperscalers (GSXUHYPR) and datacenter equipment (GSTMTDAT), long government-spending exposed ex-defense and drug-makers (GSXUGOVT) against short defense beneficiaries (GSXUDFNS).

The desk argues the datacenter debate is shifting from whether to build to who pays for incremental power generation and transmission. If policymakers converge on datacenter cost-bearing, utilities and grid operators could benefit while some datacenter project economics weaken.
Corporate tax: the midterms are unlikely to change tax law because the President can veto. 2027-28 earnings are largely insulated, and the risk is to valuations beyond 2029 if the 21% rate rises.

Other election-sensitive ideas: short Big Tech on antitrust, short investment banks and crypto-exposed equities on financial regulation, short tariff-sensitive equities (the desk sees more risk of tariffs rising than falling into early 2027), and long homebuilders on housing tax credits.
The House passed a bipartisan continuing resolution funding the government through December 11, avoiding a shutdown into November.
